questions.q: The default alignment of text in a new MS Word paragraph is:
questions.solution: New paragraphs are left-aligned (ragged right). Justify must be applied deliberately with Ctrl+J.
questions.shortcut: Word starts everything plain: left align, Calibri 11, Print Layout, portrait.

questions.q: The binary equivalent of decimal 156 is:
The decimal number 200 in hexadecimal is:
questions.shortcut: Divide by 16: 200/16 = 12 r 8 -> C8. The remainder is the last hex digit, the quotient the first.

questions.q: In Windows 10/11, pressing Win+V opens:
questions.solution: Win+V shows clipboard history, a list of recently copied items you can paste again (it must be switched on the first time). Run is Win+R and voice typing is Win+H.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl+V pastes one item; Win+V opens the whole paste history.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Plastic waste has become a global menace. **P:** It blocks drains and kills cattle that swallow it. **Q:** Many governments have banned single-use plastic bags. **R:** Yet people continue to use them for convenience. **S:** Awareness, not merely bans, is the need of the hour. **6.** Behaviour must change before laws can succeed.
questions.solution: 'It' = plastic waste → **P** (harm). **Q** (response: bans). **R** ('Yet') contrasts — usage continues. **S** concludes ('need of the hour') before S6. PQRS.
questions.shortcut: Yet-clause must follow the ban; conclusion word flags the final slot.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Separate: remember there is **'a rat' in sePArATE** — the middle vowel is a, not e. This is the most-failed word in the bank.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Millennium doubles **l and n**: mil-lenn-ium (from Latin mille + annus). The distractors each drop or move one double.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The road is wet and there are puddles everywhere; it ___ rained last night.
questions.solution: The wet road is evidence for a confident conclusion about the past → **must have + V3** (*must have rained*). *should have rained* means it was expected but did not happen; *must rained* and *ought to rained* are ungrammatical.

questions.q: Goitre is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution: **Iodine** is needed to make **thyroxine**. When it is short, the thyroid gland enlarges — **goitre**. Iron deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes M1 (narrow money) in India?
options: Currency with the public + time deposits with banks
Currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI
Currency with the public + post office savings deposits
questions.solution: **M1 = currency with the public + demand (current/savings) deposits with banks + 'other deposits' with the RBI.** Time deposits enter only M2/M3; post-office deposits sit outside M1, and M3 = M1 + time deposits (broad money).
questions.shortcut: Narrow = instantly spendable — currency plus demand deposits only.

questions.q: Who received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award in August 2026?
questions.solution: National Security Advisor **Ajit Doval** received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award on 1 August 2026 (Pune).

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Avanti** Mahajanapada (northern part)?
questions.solution: Avanti (Malwa) had two capitals — **Ujjain** in the north and **Mahishmati** in the south. Kaushambi = Vatsa, Shravasti = Kosala, Champa = Anga.

questions.q: A man invests ₹5,000 for two years. The rate of interest is 8% for the first year and 10% for the second year, compounded annually. The amount at the end of two years is:
The HCF of $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{8}{9}$ and $\frac{10}{27}$ is:
questions.shortcut: HCF of tops = 2; LCM of bottoms = 27 ⇒ 2/27.

questions.q: What is the sum of all the even factors of 72?
questions.solution:
$72 = 2^3 \times 3^2$. An even factor must contain at least one 2.
Sum $= (2 + 4 + 8)(1 + 3 + 9) = 14 \times 13 = 182$.
questions.shortcut: All factors sum to 15 × 13 = 195; odd factors sum to 13; even = 195 − 13 = 182.

questions.q: A sum of money becomes 1.44 times itself in 2 years when invested at compound interest. The annual rate of interest is:
questions.shortcut: √1.44 = 1.2 ⇒ rate 20%. (14.4% is the trap for linear thinking.)

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**8   15   49**

**7   10   39**

**6   11    ?**
questions.solution: 49 = 8² − 15; confirm 39 = 7² − 10 = 49 − 10 ✓. Rule: third = (first)² − second. So 6² − 11 = 36 − 11 = **25**. (36 is 6² without subtracting 11.)
questions.shortcut: Perfect-square third cells (49, 39? not 39... their bases 7, 7) — here the bases equal the first cell: test a² ± b.
questions.pattern: single grid, rows share a rule

questions.q: In a row of students, **Sita is 8th from the left and 21st from the right.** How many students are in the row?
questions.shortcut: Sum of the two ranks minus 1.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **ABC, KLM, RST, XZB**
questions.solution: ABC, KLM, RST are three **consecutive** letters (+1, +1). XZB steps (+2, +2) — skipped letters → **XZB**.
questions.shortcut: Runs of consecutive letters are spotted by eye; confirm one option with steps.

questions.q: In a certain code, **SUN is coded 54** (sum of alphabet positions). How is **DOG** coded?
questions.shortcut: Position sum via anchors: G = E+2 = 7, O = 15, D = E−1 = 4.
